RSA-SHA256 signature verification uses wrong hash algorithm

#### Description

```python
rsa_private_key = """-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

6+OoGU3LspowyLJVWufTHPtETpVBpdLKw5R5CL27YnwZDxTIVfYGLGi35gWHOVsQ
ZjkUS3kur7nPlW8dTlaRRVgjCOPOplYiweFcq/ts109O3slSo6pA6Md+UzYvyDVz
0txstBpS562F7HljaOQJBAPlxhgCdB5ljlVTr84YlLIDr46gZTcuymiAYslVa59M
c+0ROlUGl0srDlHkIvbtifBkPFMhV9gYsaLfmBYc5WxBmORRLeS6vuc+Vbx1OVpF

# Sign with RSA-SHA256
signature = sign_rsa_sha256_with_client(signature_base_string, MockClient(rsa_key=rsa_private_key))

# Try to verify - this should return True but returns False
request = MockRequest('POST', 'http://example.com/request', {}, signature)
result = verify_rsa_sha256(request, rsa_public_key)
print(f"Verification result: {result}")  # Expected: True, Actual: False
```

The verification fails because the function is using SHA-1 hashing internally instead of SHA-256 as expected for RSA-SHA256 signatures.
